name: Arroz Rojo, Short-Grain Adaptation — Zojirushi Neuro Fuzzy
subtitle: Zojirushi Neuro Fuzzy
description: Mexican red rice adapted for Japanese short-grain. Rice is rinsed hard and toasted in oil (pilaf-style) to fight short-grain's natural stickiness, then finished in the Neuro Fuzzy on Mixed. Expect a softer, slightly clingy grain — a Mexican-Japanese hybrid, not taquería-fluffy.

ingredients.text: 2 tsp tomato bouillon (Knorr Caldo de Tomate)

steps.text: Rinse 2 cup Japanese short-grain rice thoroughly, swirling and changing the water 3–4 times until it runs mostly clear — short-grain sheds a lot of surface starch and you want it gone. Drain very well and let sit to dry. Do NOT soak.

Heat 3 tbsp neutral oil in your stainless skillet over medium-high. Add 2 cup Japanese short-grain rice and stir constantly until the grains look chalky-white turning faintly golden and smell nutty, about 7 min. This oil coat is your main anti-clump insurance — don't shortcut it. Keep it moving so the starch doesn't scorch on stainless.
Add 1/2 medium white onion, finely diced and cook until soft and translucent, ~3 min. Add 3 garlic cloves, minced and stir 30 seconds until fragrant.

Stir in 3/4 cup tomato purée / passata, 2 tsp tomato bouillon (Knorr Caldo de Tomate), and 1/2 tsp ground cumin. Cook 2 min until it darkens slightly and goes paste-like, concentrating flavor before liquid.

Scrape everything into the Neuro Fuzzy inner pan. Add 1 1/2 cup chicken broth, 1 tsp fine salt, and 1/2 cup frozen peas & diced carrots (optional). Stir once to combine and level the rice under the liquid — then leave it alone.
Select MIXED (the takikomi-style program — handles the oil and add-ins). If unavailable, use WHITE/SUSHI. Never Quick. Start and keep the lid shut the whole cycle.
When the cycle ends, leave it on Keep Warm undisturbed for 10 min. Then fluff GENTLY with the paddle — cut and lift, don't stir — fold in 2 tbsp cilantro, chopped, and serve with 1 lime, wedged.

notes:
⚠️ UNTESTED — needs a real cook before it goes in the compendium.

Texture reality: short-grain will read softer and more cohesive than long-grain arroz rojo. The toast + oil coat is what keeps it from going full sticky-rice. If you want to push it firmer/more separate next time, the levers are (a) toast a minute longer and (b) shave another 2 tbsp off the broth.

Liquid ratio: 2.25 cups total (0.75 purée + 1.5 broth) per 2 cups rice = ~1.125:1. Deliberately lean — short-grain absorbs less than long-grain AND the sealed cooker barely evaporates. Two ways to overshoot into mush here, so I cut aggressively.

Do NOT soak: normal Japanese rice prep soaks, but soaked grains steam instead of toast. Rinse well, drain, toast dry. Skip the soak entirely for this dish.

Mixed setting is ideal here — it's essentially the takikomi-gohan program (short-grain + add-ins + seasoning), so it's native to what you're doing. Use it if you have it.

Secret weapon: tomato bouillon (Caldo de Tomate) carries the color and savory depth. Don't skip it.

Fluff gently: short-grain sheds starch and turns gluey when agitated hot. Minimal folding at the end.
